note: Topic lists follow the Pearson Edexcel IAL (2018) specification topic headings. Revision notes are original Paprivo summaries kept deliberately short: they are memory-refreshers, not full teaching notes. Topical question banks live on the linked external pages (checked live at seed time).

topics.name: Algebraic expressions
notes: Laws of indices (including fractional and negative powers) drive most P1 algebra questions.
Rationalise surds and simplify expressions like a√b before substituting — examiners reward clean working.
Expand and factorise quadratics; completing the square reveals the vertex and the minimum/maximum value at a glance.

topics.name: Equations and inequalities
notes: Quadratic formula, discriminant b²−4ac (equal roots, two roots, no real roots) and when to use it.
Solve simultaneous equations where one is quadratic — expect substitution and two solution pairs.
When multiplying an inequality by a negative number, flip the sign; sketching a quadratic helps read solutions.

topics.name: Graphs and transformations
notes: Know the shapes of y = kxⁿ for n = −2, −1, 1, 2, 3 and how n's parity changes the sketch.
Translations f(x−a)+b, reflections f(−x) and −f(x), stretches f(ax) and af(x) — describe them in words too.
Use intersections with axes and turning points as sketch anchors; label them.

topics.name: Trigonometry
notes: Right-angled trig, sine rule, cosine rule and area ½ab sin C — choose the tool from what's given.
Exact values for 30°, 45°, 60° and the graphs of sin, cos, tan (period, symmetry) are tested directly.
Solve simple trig equations in a stated interval and count all solutions using the graph's symmetry.

topics.name: Proof
notes: Distinguish proof by deduction, proof by exhaustion and disproof by counter-example — state which you're using.
Counter-example needs one value that breaks the claim; check simple values (0, 1, fraction) first.

topics.name: Algebra and functions
notes: Factor theorem and algebraic division for cubic factorisation; polynomials division remainder links.
Modulus graphs |f(x)|, f(|x|); combined transformations in the right order.
Composite fg(x) and inverse f⁻¹(x): don't forget the domain/range swap when writing the inverse.

topics.name: Coordinate geometry
notes: Line through two points: gradient, point-slope, perpendicular bisector (negative reciprocal gradient, midpoint).
Circle from (x−a)² + (y−b)² = r²; tangents are perpendicular to radii at the point of contact.
Intersection of lines and circles leads to quadratics — use the discriminant for tangent/not-touching cases.

topics.name: Sequences and series
notes: Arithmetic: a, d, nth term a+(n−1)d, sum n/2(2a+(n−1)d). Geometric: a, r, ar^(n−1), sum a(1−rⁿ)/(1−r).
Sum to infinity a/(1−r) exists only for |r|<1 — justify the inequality when asked.
Early binomial expansion of (1+x)ⁿ for small n; write full expansion with decreasing powers.

topics.name: Radians and trigonometry
notes: Radians throughout: arc length rθ, sector area ½r²θ.
Exact values and solving equations in radians; add 2π multiples when finding all solutions.
Small-angle approximations sinθ≈θ, cosθ≈1−θ²/2, tanθ≈θ inform limits questions.

topics.name: Exponentials and logarithms
notes: Graphs of eˣ, e^(−x), ln x and their intersections with lines are common modelling setups.
Laws: log(xy)=log x+log y, log(x/y)=log x−log y, log(xⁿ)=n log x — natural logs follow the same rules.
Solve aˣ=b by logs; convert y=axⁿ to log y=log a+n log x or y=abˣ to ln y=ln x·ln b+ln a for linear fits.

topics.name: Algebra and functions
notes: Partial fractions with distinct/repeated linear factors and quadratic denominators feed integration questions.
Rational functions: asymptotes, asymptote-free graphs, and using factor theorem with unknown coefficients.

topics.name: Trigonometry
notes: Reciprocal functions sec, cosec, cot and their graphs/identities; inverse functions sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹, tan⁻¹ ranges.
Compound angle, double angle and the R-form a sinθ+b cosθ=R sin(θ+α) — show working for R and α.
Most 'solve' questions combine identities; find all roots in the stated interval.

topics.name: Exponentials and logarithms
notes: Exponential growth/decay models dN/dt=kN style setups appear in both maths and applied contexts.
Take logs of reciprocal/exponential models to identify constants from straight-line data plots.

topics.name: Differentiation
notes: First principles for simple functions is examinable — memorise the limit definition.
Chain, product and quotient rules; differentiate e^x, lnx, trig and implicit-lite expressions.
Stationary points with second-derivative test; tangents and normals to curves including parametric-lite cases.

topics.name: Integration
notes: Standard integrals, reverse chain rule (ln|f(x)| forms), integration by recognition.
Definite integrals as areas; areas between a curve and a line/axes, signed areas caution.
Improper integrals appear in P3/P4 boundary questions — evaluate with limits.

topics.name: Numerical methods
notes: Locate a root by sign change over an interval and justify with a quick calculation.
Fixed-point iteration x_{n+1}=g(x_n): state the iteration, quote values to the asked accuracy.
Newton–Raphson may appear: know the formula and failure cases (derivative zero near the root).

topics.name: Algebra and functions
notes: Binomial series for any rational n: general term, validity |x|<1, expansions with bracketed x rearrangement.
Partial fractions then integrate or differentiate term by term to build series expansions.

topics.name: Trigonometry
notes: Reciprocal and inverse functions, compound/double angle proofs; R-form in modelling (max/min of asinθ+bcosθ).
Inverse trig derivatives and arcsin/arccos/arctan integrals appear with P4-heavy integration.

topics.name: Parametric equations
notes: Convert parametric ↔ cartesian by eliminating the parameter; state domain restrictions.
Parametric differentiation dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt); tangents/normals/arcs follow from it.

topics.name: Differentiation
notes: Implicit differentiation incl. normals to circles-like curves and connected rates of change.
Parametric gradients and chain-rule heavy expressions; second derivatives for concavity/inflections.
Optimisation with constraints: build a single-variable model, differentiate, verify it's a max/min.

topics.name: Integration
notes: By substitution (choose u from the inner function), by parts (LIATE heuristic), partial fractions.
Volumes of revolution around x or y axes; set limits from the geometry described.
Separable first-order differential equations with boundary conditions are a P4 staple.

topics.name: Vectors
notes: Position/direction vectors, magnitude, unit vectors, vector arrows in 2D and 3D.
Line vector equations r=a+t(b−a): read parallel vectors, find points, distances via parametric t.
Vector proofs of parallelism/collinearity are quick marks — compare scalar multiples.

topics.name: Modelling and vectors
notes: Standard modelling assumptions (light inextensible string, smooth pulley, particle) — justify or drop them when asked.
Resolve vectors into components; direction bearings and unit vectors j/î language.

topics.name: Kinematics
notes: suvat equations for constant acceleration; choose the unknown-safe equation.
Velocity–time and displacement–time graphs: gradient/area meaning, average speed vs average velocity.

topics.name: Dynamics
notes: Newton's second law F=ma in component form; systems questions need a whole-system equation plus a part equation.
Connected particles (toys on tables, pulleys, lifts): tension same magnitude along a light string.
Weight as mg, normal reactions, and when bodies lose contact (R=0 condition).

topics.name: Friction and statics
notes: F ≤ μR with equality at limiting equilibrium; direction opposes motion/impending motion.
Particles on slopes: resolve parallel and perpendicular; equilibrium vs on-point-of-sliding wording.

topics.name: Moments
notes: Moment = force × perpendicular distance; take moments about a strategic point to eliminate an unknown reaction.
Rigid-body equilibrium: sum of moments = 0 plus vertical/horizontal force balance; centre of mass position offsets.

topics.name: Projectiles
notes: Split into horizontal (constant speed) and vertical (suvat with a=−g) components; time is the shared variable.
Range, greatest height, time of flight formulae; landing at different level needs the full quadratic.

topics.name: Work, energy and power
notes: Work = force × distance in the force's direction; energy conservation incl. gains/losses on inclines.
Power = Fv; driving-train problems combine resistance, power and constant speed equations.
Work–energy principle: total work done = change in KE; include friction work as negative.

topics.name: Impulse and momentum
notes: Impulse = change in momentum = FΔt; area under a force–time graph.
Conservation of momentum for one-dimensional collisions; define a positive direction first.

topics.name: Collisions and restitution
notes: Newton's law of restitution e = speed of separation / speed of approach; e=1 elastic, e=0 inelastic.
Two-ball stacked/follow-on problems: solve both impacts in sequence; check the second collision happens.

topics.name: Centres of mass
notes: Composite laminas/shells by mass-weighted averaging of component centres (x̄=Σmx/Σm).
Tipping about an edge occurs when the centre of mass passes the support's vertical line — standard beam/plank setups.

topics.name: Variable acceleration
notes: Calculus links: a=dv/dt=d²x/dt², v=dx/dt; integrate with initial/final conditions.
Displacement vs distance demands tracking sign changes of v (stationary points).

topics.name: Elastic strings and springs
notes: Hooke's law T=λx/l for strings/springs; modulus of elasticity λ has force units.
Elastic energy stored λx²/2l powers energy-conservation questions (projos attached to springs).

topics.name: Simple harmonic motion
notes: SHM conditions and standard solutions x=a cos(ωt)+b sin(ωt); amplitude and period conversions.
Speed v=ω√(a²−x²); extrema, centre-of-oscillation, first-time-after-t style timings.
Springs+mass systems: derive ω² from the equation of motion by collecting terms.

topics.name: Centres of mass of solids
notes: Standard results: hemisphere 3r/8, cone h/4 from base, composite solids by volume-weighted averages.
Hanging/float equilibrium: vertical through centre of mass; tilt angles from geometry.

topics.name: Representation and summary of data
notes: Mean/mode/median comparisons under skew; standard deviation and variance (n and n−1 forms as specified).
Quartiles, IQR, outliers rule (Q3+1.5IQR etc); box plots, histograms, cumulative frequency reading.
Coding data (y=ax+b) scales mean and SD predictably — quick recalculation tool.

topics.name: Probability
notes: Venn/tree diagrams; addition and multiplication laws with independence checks P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B).
Conditional probability P(A|B)=P(A∩B)/P(B); convert wording to set notation carefully.

topics.name: Correlation and regression
notes: PMCC interpretation (strength, direction); correlation ≠ causation phrasing.
Regression y on x only; use it for interpolation, flag extrapolation risks; residual sum interpretation.

topics.name: Discrete random variables
notes: Probability distributions must sum to 1; find unknown constants first.
E(X), Var(X)=E(X²)−[E(X)]², and linear combos E(aX+b), Var(aX+b).

topics.name: Normal distribution
notes: Standardise Z=(X−μ)/σ; use table/norm inverse for boundaries and probabilities.
Point binomial ≈ normal when np and nq large with continuity correction where required.
Find unknown μ/σ from percentage-point equations (two equations, two unknowns).

topics.name: Binomial and Poisson distributions
notes: B(n,p) conditions (fixed n, independent trials, constant p); Poisson modelling for rates/queues.
Poisson approximation to binomial (n large, p small, np=λ) and when tables beat manual computation.
Additivity: independent Poissons with rates λ1, λ2 → Poisson(λ1+λ2).

topics.name: Continuous random variables
notes: PDF integrates to 1; CDF for P(a<X<b); find unknown k by integration limits.
Mode = PDF peak; median by integrating to 0.5; uniform distribution mean/variance by geometry.

topics.name: Sampling and estimation
notes: Unbiased estimators: mean of sample means; variance divisor (n−1) sample variance.
Sampling distribution of the mean; CLT for non-normal populations in large samples.

topics.name: Hypothesis testing
notes: State H0/H1 (one or two-tailed) and the significance level before computing.
Binomial/Poisson critical region or probability-under-H0; compare to significance and conclude in context.
Conclusions must reference the claim wording ('insufficient evidence to suggest...').

topics.name: Combinations of random variables
notes: Sums/differences: E(aX±bY), Var(aX±bY)=a²Var(X)+b²Var(Y) for independent variables.
Sums of independent normals are normal with mean and variance added; standardise for probabilities.

topics.name: Sampling distributions
notes: Central limit theorem: X̄ ~ N(μ, σ²/n) for large n whatever the population shape.
Distributions of differences of independent means/proportions underpin two-sample questions.

topics.name: Estimation and confidence
notes: Confidence intervals for the mean: z (known σ/large n) and t (unknown σ); width narrows with n².
Two-sided vs one-sided intervals; interpret '95% confident' as process coverage, not probability of one interval.

topics.name: Chi-squared tests
notes: Goodness of fit: expected counts, degrees of freedom (subtract parameters and 1), stepwise table comparison.
Contingency tables: independence test, df=(rows−1)(cols−1), merge small expected cells when required.

topics.name: Hypothesis tests for means
notes: Two-sample z/t for difference of means (independent samples), paired-sample reductions.
State assumptions (independence, normality or CLT) and conclude in the problem's wording.

topics.name: Kinematics and graphs of motion
notes: suvat for constant acceleration; displacement–time and velocity–time graphs: gradients and areas.
Projectile motion: split into independent horizontal/vertical components; time links them.
Free fall g ≈ 9.81 m/s² is measured with light gates in the standard core practical.

topics.name: Forces, Newton's laws and moments
notes: Free-body diagrams first; N1/N2/N3 phrased precisely (rate of change of momentum version is exam password).
Resolve multiple forces; equilibrium ΣF=0; moments balance for lever/plank problems.
Terminal velocity: drag increases with speed until net force is zero.

topics.name: Work, energy and power
notes: W=Fs cosθ, KE=½mv², ΔGPE=mgh; energy conservation with efficiency losses.
Power = work/time = Fv for constant-speed vehicles/hydraulics problems.

topics.name: Momentum
notes: p=mv; conservation in collisions/explosions (1D at Unit 1); impulse-momentum link appears lightly.
Momentum is a vector: assign signs before calculating.

topics.name: Fluids
notes: Density and pressure (p=hρg for columns); upthrust = weight of displaced fluid.
Laminar vs turbulent flow; viscosity definition η=F/A ÷ velocity gradient.
Stokes' law F=6πηrv for terminal velocity of spheres; experimental determination of η.

topics.name: Materials
notes: Hooke's law F=kΔx up to the limit of proportionality; force–extension energy area = work stored.
Stress σ=F/A, strain ε=Δx/x, Young modulus E=σ/ε; brittle vs ductile behaviour on σ–ε graphs.
Springs in series/parallel combine stiffnesses like 1/k and k sums.

topics.name: The nature of light
notes: Photon energy E=hf=hc/λ; intensity relates to photon rate.
Photoelectric effect: threshold frequency, KEmax=hf−φ — evidence for quantised EM radiation.
Electron energy levels give line spectra; express transitions as ΔE=hf.

topics.name: Waves
notes: v=fλ, wavefronts/rays; progressive vs stationary waves (nodes/antinodes, strings experiment).
Refraction/Snell's law, critical angle and total internal reflection; optical fibres.
Polarisation only for transverse waves; diffraction/interference (path difference, coherence).

topics.name: Wave-particle duality
notes: de Broglie λ=h/p for electrons; diffraction evidence for matter waves.
Compare photon (light quanta) and electron behaviour; link ideas to the electron microscope.

topics.name: DC electricity
notes: I=Q/t, V=W/Q; Ohm's law and I–V characteristics for filament (temperature effect) and diodes.
Resistivity ρ=RA/L; series/parallel resistor networks, potential dividers and power P=VI.
EMF ε=I(R+r): internal resistance reduces terminal p.d.; efficiency and short-circuit reasoning.

topics.name: Measurement techniques
notes: Instrument choice and resolution (ruler, vernier, micrometer, stopwatch, sensors); avoid parallax error.
Oscillation timing: time many cycles and divide to cut timing reaction error.

topics.name: Uncertainties and errors
notes: Absolute/percentage uncertainty combination for sums (add absolute) and products (add percentage).
Random vs systematic errors; repeats reduce random uncertainty, calibration fixes systematic.

topics.name: Graphical analysis
notes: Log-log/ln plots linearise power/exponential relations; extract gradient→constants.
Error bars and best/worst gradient lines give uncertainty in gradients and intercepts.

topics.name: Core practicals recap
notes: Know methods/variables for mechanics (g by free fall), materials (Young modulus) and waves (standing waves) practicals.
Be ready to critique method: control variables, safe layout, and how to improve precision.

topics.name: Further mechanics
notes: 2D momentum conservation with component equations; impulse FΔt=Δp and force–time graphs.
Elastic vs inelastic collisions via KE comparison; restitution not required at Unit 4.

topics.name: Circular motion
notes: Angular speed ω=2πf, v=ωr; centripetal force F=mv²/r with real examples (banking, satellites-lite).
Identify the force providing centripetal acceleration in each context — it's always a real force.

topics.name: Electric fields
notes: E=F/q; field between parallel plates E=V/d; point-charge field E=kQ/r² (proportional reasoning acceptable).
Work done moving charge W=QΔV; equipotentials ⊥ field lines sketches.

topics.name: Capacitors
notes: Q=CV, energy ½CV²; series/parallel combinations.
Exponential charge/discharge with time constant τ=RC; read capacitor graphs for τ and initial gradient RC reasoning.

topics.name: Magnetic fields
notes: F=BIL sinθ and F=BQv for moving charges; Fleming's left-hand rule direction work.
Charged particle in circular path r=p/BQ; motor effect and simple induction ideas.

topics.name: Nuclear and particle physics
notes: Quark model (u/d/s combinations), baryons vs mesons; beta decay and the neutrino story.
Mass-energy E=mc² in fusion/fission; particle accelerators raise momentum → de Broglie wavelength shrinks.

topics.name: Thermodynamics
notes: Specific heat capacity Q=mcΔθ and specific latent heat Q=mL during phase change.
Ideal gas: pV=nRT (or NkT), kinetic theory pV=⅓Nm(c²)rms; temperature as mean KE.

topics.name: Nuclear decay
notes: Activity A=λN, decay N=N₀e^(−λt), half-life t½=ln2/λ; interpret decay graphs.
Binding energy per nucleon curve explains fission/fusion energy release; mass defect and E=mc².

topics.name: Oscillations
notes: SHM: a=−ω²x; solutions x=A cos(ωt+φ), v=±ω√(A²−x²); period independent of amplitude.
Damping reduces amplitude; resonance at driving frequency ≈ natural frequency (with light damping).

topics.name: Gravitational fields
notes: g=GM/r²; field strength vs potential; equipotentials; weightlessness phrasing.
Orbital motion: gravitational force = centripetal; T² ∝ r³ for circular orbits.

topics.name: Astrophysics and cosmology
notes: Stefan–Boltzmann L=σAT⁴ and Wien λmaxT=const; luminosity/brightness with inverse-square.
HR diagram, stellar lifecycle (main sequence → giants → white dwarf/neutron star/black hole).
Redshift and Hubble's law v=H₀d give the expanding-universe argument; receding/blueshifted spectra.

topics.name: Planning investigations
notes: Identify independent/dependent/control variables and justify the measurement instrument for each.
Write a workable method incl. safety and how graphs will be used to reach the conclusion.

topics.name: Analysis and evaluation
notes: Linearise data, compute gradient/intercept with uncertainties, and compare to accepted values.
Percent difference judgement plus improvement suggestions (repeats, sensors, reducing systematic error).

topics.name: Core practicals recap
notes: A2-era practicals: capacitors discharge, oscillations (g by pendulum-style), fields and thermodynamics experiments.
Expect critique-style questions: what would you change and why, with quantitative reasoning.

units.name: Structure, Bonding and Introduction to Organic Chemistry

topics.name: Formulae, equations and amounts of substance
notes: Moles n=m/Mr, n=CV for solutions, gas volume n=V/24 (dm³, RTP); ideal gas equation appears too.
Balanced equations from titration data; limiting reagent, percentage yield and atom economy.
Avogadro constant conversions between particles and moles.

topics.name: Atomic structure and the periodic table
notes: Electron configuration incl. 4s-before-3d fill and ion exceptions; isotopes and relative mass.
First ionisation energy trends (across period and down group) with sub-shell explanations.
Period 3 oxides' bonding and acid-base character link structure to properties.

topics.name: Bonding and structure
notes: Ionic/covalent/metallic bonding; shapes from electron-pair repulsion incl. lone-pair effects.
Polarity (dipoles) and IMF ranking: London < dipole-dipole < hydrogen bonding; link to bp/melting.
Giant structures: diamond vs graphite vs metals explain conductivity/hardness.

topics.name: Introductory organic chemistry and alkanes
notes: IUPAC naming, structural/isomer counting; functional group recognition chart.
Crude oil: fractional distillation, cracking; combustion completeness and pollutants.
Free-radical substitution mechanism (initiation/propagation/termination) with conditions.

topics.name: Alkenes
notes: Double-bond reactivity: electrophilic addition of HX/Br2 with major/minor product Markovnikov-lite logic.
Addition polymerisation; addition vs substitution contrast.
Test for unsaturation (bromine water decolourises); industrial hydrogenation/ hydration basics.

units.name: Energetics, Group Chemistry, Halogenoalkanes and Alcohols

topics.name: Energetics
notes: Enthalpy level diagrams, exothermic/endothermic sign conventions; ΔH from average bond enthalpies vs Hess cycles.
Calorimetry q=mcΔT; sources of error and improved-insulation setups.
Hess's law cycles with formation/combustion data — keep signs consistent.

topics.name: Intermolecular forces
notes: Rank London/dipole-dipole/H-bonds; justify boiling points of hydrides and isomer pairs.
Solubility reasoning: 'like dissolves like' plus H-bonding exceptions.

topics.name: Redox chemistry and groups 1, 2 and 7
notes: Oxidation numbers and half-equations; oxidising/reducing agent identification.
Group 2 reactivity/trends (sulfates, hydroxides solubility); flame tests.
Group 7 displacement and disproportionation; chlorine water treatment debate points.

topics.name: Introduction to kinetics and equilibria
notes: Collision theory: concentration/temperature/surface-area/catalyst effects; Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution sketching.
Dynamic equilibrium with Le Chatelier predictions; Kc expression and ICE-table calculations.

topics.name: Halogenoalkanes, alcohols and spectra
notes: SN1/SN2 mechanisms and rates with primary/tertiary halogenoalkanes; hydrolysis experiment with AgNO3.
Alcohol oxidation: primary→aldehyde→acid, secondary→ketone, tertiary resistant; distill vs reflux.
Mass spectra (m/z fragments, M+ peak) and IR (bond vibrations, O-H/C=O regions) identification.

topics.name: Core techniques
notes: Titration procedure with indicators and concordant titres; burette/pipette use and uncertainty reading.
Heating under reflux, distillation, recrystallisation, melting point purity testing.

topics.name: Analysis and evaluation
notes: Quantitative uncertainties in measured volumes/masses and % error comparison.
Critique and improve methods: control variables, drying/recrystallising steps, yield vs purity trade-offs.

topics.name: Qualitative tests
notes: Cation/anion/gas tests: flame colours, AgNO3 halides, carbonate effervescence, sulfate barium, ammonia tests.
Organic tests for unsaturation and functional groups with expected observations stated precisely.

units.name: Rates, Equilibria and Further Organic Chemistry

topics.name: Kinetics
notes: Rate equations, orders (0/1/2) and rate constant k with units; initial-rates method and clock reactions.
Rate-determining step and plausible mechanisms from order data; Arrhenius equation ln k = −Ea/RT + ln A linearisation.

topics.name: Entropy and energetics
notes: Entropy signs/change reasoning; ΔS = ΣS(products) − ΣS(reactants).
Gibbs energy ΔG=ΔH−TΔS; spontaneity temperature thresholds and decomposition feasibility.

topics.name: Chemical equilibria
notes: Kp/Kc calculations incl. partial pressures and mole fractions; Le Chatelier with industrial compromise (Haber/ammonia).

topics.name: Acid-base equilibria
notes: Ka, pKa, Kw=10⁻¹⁴ at 298K; pH of strong/weak acids and bases.
Buffers: ratio reasoning and addition response; titration curves and indicator choice.

topics.name: Carbonyls, carboxylic acids and chirality
notes: Aldehyde/ketone tests (Tollens, Fehling, 2,4-DNPH); nucleophilic addition mechanism.
Carboxylic acid acidity and derivatives (acyl chlorides, esters, anhydrides) reactions.
Optical isomerism with chiral centres; optical activity/subsequent racemisation from SN1 mechanisms.

units.name: Transition Metals and Organic Nitrogen Chemistry

topics.name: Redox equilibria
notes: Standard electrode potentials E°; cell EMF = E°(cathode)−E°(anode) and spontaneity.
Predict reactions with E° data; disproportionation and oxidising strength ordering.

topics.name: Transition metals
notes: Variable oxidation states; complex ions with ligand substitution, colour from d-orbital splitting (…simplified as IAL allows).
Reactions of Cu²⁺/Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺/Cr³⁺ with NaOH/NH3; catalysis examples incl. heterogeneous contact process.

topics.name: Arenes
notes: Benzene delocalised model vs Kekulé; stability via ΔHhydrogenation comparison.
Electrophilic substitution: nitration (NO2⁺) and halogenation (AlCl3/FeBr3 catalysts); directing effects (2/4 vs 3).

topics.name: Organic nitrogen compounds
notes: Amines basicity, preparation; amide formation; diazonium coupling to azo dyes (overview-level).
Amino acids zwitterions, isoelectric points; peptide bonds and hydrolysis of proteins.

topics.name: Organic synthesis
notes: Multi-step routes: choose reagents/conditions between functional groups; protection where needed.
Purity/chirality considerations in synthesis; green-chemistry-flavoured justification questions.

topics.name: Advanced core practicals
notes: Redox titrations (e.g. Fe²⁺/MnO4⁻) with electron-count stoichiometry.
Organic preparation/purification and rate-measurement experiments at A2 demand.

topics.name: Evaluation style
notes: Quantify uncertainties in multi-step measurements and judge the dominant error source.
Suggest improvements tied to identified errors (thermostatted vessels, calibration, recording frequency).

topics.name: Molecules, transport and health
notes: Water's properties (H-bonding) underpin transport; carbohydrate/lipid/protein structures and tests (Benedict's, iodine, biuret).
Cardiovascular system: heart structure, cardiac cycle, blood vessels; atherosclerosis and CVD risk factors.
Diet: energy balance, BMI/waist-hip, food tests; blood pressure reading interpretation.

topics.name: Membranes, proteins, DNA and gene expression
notes: Fluid mosaic model; diffusion/osmosis/active transport with experimental contexts (beetroot, water potential).
Protein structure levels and enzyme action (induced fit), factors affecting rate with graph reading.
DNA/RNA structure, semiconservative replication, transcription/translation and the genetic code.

topics.name: Cell structure, reproduction and development
notes: Eukaryotic organelles vs prokaryotes; light/electron microscopy magnification/resolution calculations.
Mitosis stages and meiosis with gamete variation; fertilisation and early development in mammals/plants.

topics.name: Plant structure and function, biodiversity and conservation
notes: Plant tissues (xylem, phloem, sclerenchyma); transpiration/cohesion-tension and transport experiments.
Classification hierarchy and the five-kingdom/three-domain debate; species concepts.
Biodiversity indices (Simpson's), niche concepts, conservation strategies and seed banks.

topics.name: Core techniques
notes: Microscope practicals, enzyme-rate experiments, membrane permeability, water potential serial dilutions.
Data handling: tables, graphs and Unit 1/2 variable control.

topics.name: Analysis and evaluation
notes: Represent results and identify anomalies; explain reliability via repeats.
Suggest improvements mapped to specific weaknesses rather than generic answers.

topics.name: Statistical tests (light)
notes: Unit-level significance basics; be comfortable with mean comparisons and simple significance reasoning.

topics.name: Energy flow, ecosystems and the environment
notes: Photosynthesis: light-dependent/independent reactions and limiting factors experiments.
Respiration overview (glycolysis → link/Krebs/ETC) and RQ calculations.
Ecosystems: trophic levels, energy transfer efficiency, pyramids; succession and population change (abiotic/biotic).

topics.name: Microbiology, immunity and forensics
notes: Bacterial growth curves and culturing technique (aseptic); antibiotic action/resistance mechanisms.
Pathogens and disease (TB, HIV); immune response: phagocytes, T/B lymphocytes, antibodies, memory.
Vaccination/time-course graphs; forensic techniques incl. DNA profiling, PCR basics and time-of-death factors.

units.name: Respiration, Internal Environment, Coordination and Gene Technology

topics.name: Respiration, muscles and the internal environment
notes: Respiration detail: ATP yield, chemiosmotic theory, mitochondrial adaptations; respirometer experiments.
Muscle structure: sliding filament with actin/myosin/calcium role; slow vs fast fibres.
Homeostasis: thermoregulation loops; kidneys: ultrafiltration/selective reabsorption/osmoregulation with ADH.

topics.name: Coordination, response and gene technology
